title: Noah Takes the Throne
summary: Zeniff confers the kingdom upon Noah, who begins to reign and does not follow his father’s ways.

explicit_facts.text: Zeniff confers the kingdom upon Noah, one of his sons, and Noah begins to reign in his stead.
Noah does not walk in his father’s ways or keep God’s commandments, and follows the desires of his own heart.
Noah has many wives and concubines and causes his people to commit sin and wickedness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A transfer of royal authority can be shown with Noah and Zeniff together.
unspecified_visual_details: Their clothing, the throne, the ceremony, and the precise location are not described.

narration.text: Zeniff conferred the kingdom upon Noah

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict specific sinful acts or assign names or identities to Noah’s wives and concubines.

title: The Tax
summary: Noah imposes a one-fifth tax on possessions, metals, livestock, and grain to support himself, his household, and the priests and their households.

explicit_facts.text: Noah levies a tax of one fifth of the people’s possessions, specified metals, fatlings, and grain.
The tax supports Noah, his wives and concubines, and his priests and their wives and concubines.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A tax collection may be represented by goods being gathered from the people.
unspecified_visual_details: The collection method, appearance of the goods, and participants’ individual identities are not specified.

narration.text: he laid a tax of one fifth part

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the tax as a specific coin payment; the text lists multiple kinds of goods and possessions.

title: New Priests
summary: Noah removes the priests consecrated by his father and consecrates new priests; taxes support the new priests’ idolatry and wickedness while the people labor.

explicit_facts.text: Noah removes the priests consecrated by his father and consecrates new ones, described as prideful.
Taxes support the priests in laziness, idolatry, and wickedness; the people labor exceedingly to support iniquity.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The removal and replacement of priests may be shown as a change in who occupies priestly positions.
unspecified_visual_details: The ceremony, the priests’ names, and the appearance of any objects of worship are not described.

narration.text: the people labor exceedingly to support iniquity

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the specific content of the people’s sins or depict an undescribed idol.

title: Flattering Words
summary: The people become idolatrous after being deceived by the king’s and priests’ flattering words.

explicit_facts.text: The people become idolatrous because the king and priests deceive them with vain and flattering words.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The king and priests may be shown addressing listeners.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, gestures, and the words spoken are not specified.

narration.text: they did speak flattering things unto them

prohibited_inventions: Do not create direct dialogue: the verse summarizes their speech without giving its words.

title: Buildings and Palace
summary: King Noah builds many elegant, spacious buildings, ornamenting them with fine woodwork and precious materials. He also builds a spacious palace with a throne in its midst.

explicit_facts.text: King Noah built many elegant and spacious buildings ornamented with fine woodwork, precious things, gold, silver, iron, brass, ziff, and copper.
He also built a spacious palace with a throne in its midst; the palace and throne were of fine wood and ornamented with gold, silver, and precious things.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The throne can be shown inside the palace, with the stated wood and ornamentation visible.
unspecified_visual_details: The buildings' architectural style and dimensions are unspecified.
King Noah's appearance is unspecified.

narration.text: And he also built him a spacious palace, and a throne in the midst thereof

prohibited_inventions: Do not name a location or add materials not supplied by these verses.
Do not depict King Noah personally performing construction work as an explicit event.

title: Temple Ornamentation
summary: He causes his workmen to make fine work within the temple. He ornaments the high priests’ seats with pure gold and causes a breastwork to be built before them.

explicit_facts.text: He causes his workmen to make fine work within the temple using fine wood, copper, and brass.
The seats set apart for the high priests are above the other seats and are ornamented with pure gold.
He causes a breastwork to be built before those seats so the high priests can rest their bodies and arms upon it while speaking lying and vain words to his people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The elevated seats, gold ornamentation, and breastwork can be shown together within the temple.
unspecified_visual_details: The temple’s location and overall design, the workmen’s tools, and the appearance of the people are unspecified.

narration.text: the seats which were set apart for the high priests

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the unnamed man as Noah from these verses alone.
Do not invent the words spoken by the high priests.

title: Tower Near the Temple
summary: He built a very high tower near the temple. From its top, he could overlook Shilom, Shemlon, and the surrounding land.
locations: Land of Shilom (overlooked from the tower)
Land of Shemlon (overlooked from the tower)

explicit_facts.text: He built a very high tower near the temple.
The tower was high enough that he could stand atop it and overlook Shilom, Shemlon, and the surrounding land.
Shemlon was possessed by the Lamanites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The tower rises above nearby structures or terrain.
unspecified_visual_details: The tower’s materials and design are unspecified.
The appearance of the temple and distant lands is unspecified.

narration.text: he built a tower near the temple

prohibited_inventions: Do not place the tower in Shilom; the temple’s location is not given.
Do not name the builder from this verse alone.
Do not depict him standing on the tower as an event; the verse says he could do so.

title: Buildings in Shilom
summary: Noah uses the wealth gained through taxation to build many buildings in Shilom and a great tower on the hill north of Shilom.

explicit_facts.text: Noah has many buildings built in Shilom and a great tower built on the hill north of Shilom.
The hill had been a resort for the children of Nephi when they fled from the land.
Noah uses riches obtained by taxing his people for this building.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The buildings and tower may be shown as construction or completed structures.
unspecified_visual_details: The people involved in construction, building designs, and the historical flight are not described visually.

narration.text: he did do with the riches which he obtained by the taxation of his people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The earlier resort and flight are mentioned as background, not narrated as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the children of Nephi fleeing in this scene.

title: Riotous Living
summary: Noah sets his heart on riches and spends time in riotous living; he plants vineyards, builds wine-presses, and makes abundant wine.

explicit_facts.text: Noah sets his heart on riches and spends time in riotous living with his wives and concubines; his priests spend time with harlots.
Noah plants vineyards, builds wine-presses, and makes wine in abundance; he and his people become wine-bibbers.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Vineyards and wine-presses may be shown as described.
unspecified_visual_details: The nature of riotous living and the appearance or identities of the people are unspecified.

narration.text: he planted vineyards round about in the land

prohibited_inventions: Do not portray specific sexual acts or infer that wine is being consumed in the vineyard.

title: Raids and Insufficient Guards
summary: Lamanites began attacking small numbers of Noah’s people in fields and while they tended flocks. Noah then sent guards around the land, but too few; Lamanites killed them and drove many flocks out of the land.

explicit_facts.text: Lamanites began coming upon small numbers of Noah’s people and killing them in fields and while they tended flocks.
King Noah sent guards around the land to keep the Lamanites off, but did not send enough.
The Lamanites came upon the guards, killed them, and drove many flocks out of the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A field attack may show Lamanites confronting people tending flocks.
A later view may show flocks being driven away; it should not imply the guards were already present during the earlier attacks.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact terrain, number of people and animals, clothing, and weapons are unspecified.

narration.text: to slay them in their fields, and while they were tending their flocks.
And king Noah sent guards round about the land to keep them off; but he did not send a sufficient number

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The attacks and the sending of guards occur in sequence, not as one simultaneous event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not label the land as Shilom or give unnamed people invented names or biographies.
Do not show gore or invent a battle outcome beyond the stated deaths and loss of flocks.

title: The Armies Return
summary: King Noah's armies return rejoicing in their spoil after a victory. They boast in their own strength, saying that their fifty could stand against thousands of the Lamanites.

explicit_facts.text: King Noah sent his armies against an opposing group; the verse says they were driven back, or they drove the opposing group back for a time.
The armies returned rejoicing in their spoil.
After the victory, they became prideful and boasted that their fifty could stand against thousands of the Lamanites.
They delighted in blood and the shedding of their brethren's blood, which the verse attributes to the wickedness of their king and priests.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The returning armies may be shown together with unspecified spoil.
Their rejoicing and boasting may be shown through their expressions and gestures.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and appearance of the armies are unspecified.
The contents of the spoil are unspecified.

narration.text: they returned rejoicing in their spoil.
their fifty could stand against thousands of the Lamanites;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The claim about fifty standing against thousands is reported boasting, not a demonstrated event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not place King Noah or the Lamanites physically in the return scene without textual support.
Do not invent the spoil's contents, a location, combat details, or gore.
Do not present the reported boast as verbatim spoken dialogue.

title: Abinadi Prophesies
summary: Abinadi goes among the people and prophesies the Lord’s warning that they must repent or be delivered into the hands of their enemies and brought into bondage.

explicit_facts.text: Abinadi goes among the people and begins to prophesy, saying the Lord has commanded him to deliver a warning.
The Lord warns that unless the people repent, he will deliver them into their enemies’ hands and they will be brought into bondage and afflicted.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Abinadi addressing a group of listeners is supported.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise location, audience size, and Abinadi’s appearance are unspecified.

narration.text: Go forth, and say unto this people
except they repent I will visit them in mine anger

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord’s warning is quoted as Abinadi’s prophecy; the Lord is not described as visibly appearing.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the prophesied bondage as occurring in this scene.

title: The Warning Continues
summary: Abinadi’s prophecy continues: the Lord says the people will know him and warns that, unless they repent, none but the Lord Almighty will deliver them from bondage.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says the people will know that he is their God and describes himself as jealous, visiting the iniquities of his people.
Unless they repent and turn to the Lord, the people will be brought into bondage, and none but the Lord Almighty will deliver them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The prophecy may continue as off-screen speech over Abinadi addressing the people.
unspecified_visual_details: The audience’s response and any visible divine presence are unspecified.

narration.text: none shall deliver them, except it be the Lord the Almighty God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses report prophetic words, not a visible divine appearance or present bondage.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray God appearing or the people already in bondage.

title: A Call to Repent
summary: Abinadi’s prophecy warns that the Lord will be slow to hear the people’s cries and will not deliver them unless they repent in sackcloth and ashes and cry mightily to him.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says he will be slow to hear the people’s cries and will allow them to be smitten by their enemies.
Unless they repent in sackcloth and ashes and cry mightily to the Lord, he will not hear their prayers or deliver them from afflictions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Abinadi may continue speaking to the people; the verses do not depict the foretold suffering.
unspecified_visual_details: No act of repentance or enemy attack is narrated here.

narration.text: except they repent in sackcloth and ashes

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The conditional warning is prophetic speech, not an event happening in the scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the people in sackcloth, under attack, or praying; these are conditions or predictions, not narrated actions.

title: The People Turn on Abinadi
summary: After Abinadi speaks, the people become angry and seek to take his life, but the Lord delivers him out of their hands.

explicit_facts.text: After Abinadi speaks, the people become wroth and seek to take his life.
The Lord delivers Abinadi out of their hands.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people moving to seize Abinadi may illustrate their attempt, with Abinadi escaping their grasp.
unspecified_visual_details: The manner of his deliverance and whether it is visibly miraculous are not described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the mechanics of the deliverance or show a supernatural figure.

title: Noah Orders Abinadi’s Death
summary: After hearing Abinadi’s words, King Noah becomes angry, questions Abinadi’s authority and the Lord, and commands that Abinadi be brought to him so he may slay him.

explicit_facts.text: Noah hears the words Abinadi spoke to the people and becomes angry.
Noah questions Abinadi’s judgment of him and his people and asks who the Lord is to bring affliction upon them.
Noah commands that Abinadi be brought to him so he may slay him.
Noah says Abinadi spoke to stir up anger and contention among his people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Noah’s anger may be visible as he speaks.
Noah may direct his command toward people whose identities are not shown.
unspecified_visual_details: The location is unspecified.
The identities and number of people addressed by Noah are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Who is Abinadi, that I and my people should be judged of him, or who is the Lord, that shall bring upon my people such great affliction?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Noah

spoken_dialogue.text: I command you to bring Abinadi hither, that I may slay him,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Noah

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Noah’s claim about Abinadi stirring up anger and contention is his stated accusation, not an independently established event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the command recipients as servants.
Do not show Abinadi present or depict his capture or death.
Do not depict the Lord appearing.

title: Hardened Hearts
summary: The people harden their hearts against Abinadi’s words and continue seeking to take him; Noah hardens his heart against the Lord’s word and does not repent.

explicit_facts.text: The people’s eyes are blinded; they harden their hearts against Abinadi’s words and seek from then on to take him.
Noah hardens his heart against the word of the Lord and does not repent of his evil doings.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people may be shown looking hostile or resolute; the verse does not describe literal blindness.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s precise actions, gathering place, and any attempt to seize Abinadi in this verse are unspecified.

narration.text: they hardened their hearts against the words of Abinadi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “Their eyes were blinded” is figurative in this context and should not be depicted as literal blindness.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal blindness or invent a new attempt to capture Abinadi.
